rem:observable-subcategory-remark:
Remark Observability, complement and components of the observable subcategory. Observability. One requires a non-degenerate Frobenius pairing to define degree-0 measurements. When A_0|_{\mathcal{S}} = 0, the pairing degenerates on the lowest floor of the brane tower and no degree-0 observable is well-defined. The subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} defines the regime where the full observational apparatus functions.

Complement. The complement \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) \setminus \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) consists of configurations with A_0 = 0. These are the jet horizons and big bang states.

Connected components. The connected components \pi_0(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}) are the aeons. Each aeon is a maximal connected full subcategory of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}. It encompasses all light cones accessible without crossing a jet horizon.
def:aeon: Definition Aeon. Let \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) be the observable subcategory of the category of finite bundles over the projective line. An aeon is a connected component of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)).
rem:aeon-remark:
Remark Aeons as unions of light cones. An aeon \mathcal{A} is a maximal full subcategory of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} such that a zigzag of morphisms (flow maps, inclusions, or their inverses) connects any two objects \mathcal{S} and \mathcal{S}' without leaving \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}. Every light cone forms a directed diagram within the aeon. The aeon unions all light cones that connect without crossing a jet horizon.

Maximality. The connected-component definition guarantees maximality automatically. No larger subcategory of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} containing \mathcal{A} is connected. One avoids defining an explicit interval (a, b) \subset \mathbb{Z}. Instead, one defines the aeon over the full categorical structure, naturally encompassing all intersecting light cones.
def:aeon-boundary:
Definition Boundary of an aeon. Let \mathcal{A} be an aeon —a connected component of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)).

The boundary \partial\mathcal{A} of an aeon is the set of objects \mathcal{S} \in \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)) that are limits of diagrams in \mathcal{A} but do not themselves lie in \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}:

  \partial\mathcal{A}
  = 
  \overline{\mathcal{A}} \setminus \mathcal{A}^{\circ}
  \subset
  \bigl\{
    \mathcal{S} : \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) = 0
  \bigr\}.

Each boundary object represents a jet horizon or a big bang state . One defines the boundary datum at \mathcal{S} \in \partial\mathcal{A} as the colimit of the degree \geq 1 data over all diagrams in \mathcal{A} approaching \mathcal{S}. This is the CMB boundary datum \mathrm{CMB}(\partial\mathcal{A}) .
def:aeon-adjacency:
Definition Aeon adjacency. Let \mathcal{A} and \mathcal{A}' be aeons with boundaries \partial\mathcal{A} and \partial\mathcal{A}'. The aeons \mathcal{A} and \mathcal{A}' are adjacent, and stand in aeon adjacency, if their boundaries share a common object:

  \partial\mathcal{A} \cap \partial\mathcal{A}' \neq \varnothing.
rem:aeon-adjacency-remark: Remark Aeon adjacency as a cosmological hand-off. The shared boundary object simultaneously represents the terminal horizon of one aeon and the initial configuration of the next. It categorically realises one cosmological cycle handing off to the next.
rem:observable-beable-correspondence:
Remark Beable-algebra correspondence: degree-0 algebra as 't Hooft's beable algebra. 't Hooft's Cellular Automaton Interpretation of quantum mechanics [thooft2016] introduces the notion of a beable algebra \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{beable}} — a maximal commuting subalgebra of observables whose simultaneous eigenstates constitute the ontological basis of the underlying deterministic aether. The framework's observable subcategory \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) realises this notion structurally, with the following dictionary:

't Hooft (CAI) QOU (this framework)
beable algebra \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{beable}} degree-0 algebra \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0)
ontological basis simultaneous eigenstates of the algebra \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0)
"elements of reality" degree-0 observables
beable axiom (maximal commuting) non-degeneracy of the Frobenius pairing on A_0
epistemological / templated states degree-> 0 floors of the brane tower

Structural vs. axiomatic. 't Hooft posits the beable algebra as an additional axiom — one must specify, separately from the dynamics, which subalgebra of operators is ontological. The QOU observable subcategory removes this axiomatic freedom: the degree-0 algebra \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) is determined by the bundle data \mathcal{S}, and the non-triviality condition \Gamma(\mathcal{S}, A_0) \neq 0 is a property of the bundle, not a choice. The ontological basis is therefore not an input to the theory but a derived feature of the categorical structure.

Maximality. 't Hooft's beable algebra is by construction maximal commuting (elements outside it fail to commute with some beable). In QOU the corresponding maximality is the statement that the degree-0 algebra is the maximal floor of the brane tower on which the Frobenius pairing is non-degenerate; higher floors (A_n for n \geq 1) carry richer braided structure and fail the commutativity required for simultaneous measurement. The filtration A_0 \subset A_1 \subset \cdots ordered by Frobenius non-degeneracy is the categorical analogue of the beable / epistemic split.

Epistemic states as higher floors. The states 't Hooft calls epistemological (templated superpositions used by the observer to encode partial knowledge) correspond in QOU to elements of the higher brane-tower floors restricted to \mathcal{S} for n \geq 1 — well-defined as categorical data, but not directly measurable since the Frobenius pairing is degenerate or absent at those floors. Projection to A_0 is the QOU realisation of 't Hooft's "epistemic-to-ontological" projector.

Consequence: no superselection axiom. 't Hooft requires a separate superselection postulate to forbid coherent superpositions across beable sectors. In QOU this follows automatically from the categorical structure: the connected components \pi_0(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}) — the aeons — are precisely the superselection sectors, and morphisms between distinct aeons are forbidden by the jet-horizon structure rather than by an additional axiom.
def:horizon-functor:
Definition Horizon functor. Let \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V)) be the observable subcategory, and let \pi_0(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}) be its set of connected components (the aeons). The horizon functor is the map

  \partial \colon 
  \pi_0\!\bigl(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V))\bigr)
  \longrightarrow 
  \mathcal{P}\!\bigl(
    \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V))
    \setminus
    \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V))
  \bigr)

sending each aeon \mathcal{A} to its boundary, the set of configurations \mathcal{S} that appear as limits of diagrams in \mathcal{A} but have A_0|_{\mathcal{S}} = 0:

  \partial(\mathcal{A})
  = 
  \bigl\{
    \mathcal{S} \in \mathrm{Bun} \setminus \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}
    : 
    \mathcal{S} = \varinjlim D
    \text{ for some directed diagram } D \subset \mathcal{A}
  \bigr\}.
rem:horizon-functor-remark:
Remark Horizons, adjacency and the torsion flow. Every element of \partial(\mathcal{A}) defines a jet horizon.

Functoriality. If \mathcal{A} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{A}' is an inclusion of connected components, then \mathcal{A} = \mathcal{A}' by maximality, and \partial acts as the identity. For adjacent aeons \mathcal{A} and \mathcal{A}', the intersection \partial(\mathcal{A}) \cap \partial(\mathcal{A}') \neq \varnothing. These shared boundary objects specify the loci where the CCC transition occurs.

Relation to the torsion flow. The torsion flow \Phi_t^q provides an endofunctor of \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)). Within an aeon, \Phi_t^q restricts to an endofunctor of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} (preserving A_0 \neq 0). The horizon \partial(\mathcal{A}) constitutes the set of fixed points of the limiting behaviour \Phi_t^q \to \partial as t approaches the aeon boundary.
def:cmb-functor:
Definition CMB functor. To aggregate the cosmic microwave background across an entire boundary, one promotes the pointwise boundary datum to a functor.

Let \partial be the horizon functor and let A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots be the brane tower . The CMB functor maps each aeon \mathcal{A} to the colimit of the degree \geq 1 jet quotients over its boundary. One defines this as the composition:

  \mathrm{CMB}
   \colon 
  \pi_0\!\bigl(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}\bigr)
  \xrightarrow{\partial}
  \mathcal{P}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Bun} \setminus \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}\bigr)
  \xrightarrow{\varinjlim (A_1/A_0 \oplus A_2/A_0)}
  \mathbf{Mod}_R.

Evaluated on an aeon \mathcal{A}, the functor yields:

  \mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{A})
  = 
  \varinjlim_{\mathcal{S} \in \partial(\mathcal{A})}
  \bigl(A_1/A_0 \oplus A_2/A_0\bigr)\big|_{\mathcal{S}}.

The target category \mathbf{Mod}_R consists of R-modules corresponding to sections of the jet quotient sheaves over the boundary.

Factor Jet degree Content
\varinjlim (A_1/A_0)\vert_{\partial\mathcal{A}} 1 Linear transport: winding modes, first-order correlations
\varinjlim (A_2/A_0)\vert_{\partial\mathcal{A}} 2 Curvature: linking modes, power spectrum

One takes the colimit over the directed system of all diagrams in \mathcal{A} converging to boundary objects. This aggregates the degree \geq 1 data from every light cone reaching the boundary, not just a single computation sequence.

For a single boundary object \mathcal{S}_0 \in \partial(\mathcal{A}), the pointwise CMB \mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{S}_0) = (A_1/A_0, A_2/A_0)|_{\mathcal{S}_0} is the stalk of the CMB functor at \mathcal{S}_0. The full CMB functor is the sheafification over the entire boundary.

By conformal invariance , the CMB functor does not depend on the choice of generator for the horizon ideal \mathfrak{h} \subset A_0. It depends solely on the vanishing locus—the conformal class of A_0.
rem:aeon-boundary-generates-chart:
Remark Aeon recycling: \Phi_1^q \circ \mathrm{CMB} lands in \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}. Conjecture (Aeon recycling). Let \mathrm{CMB} be the CMB functor . Let \Phi_1^q denote the first Planck step of the torsion flow , and let \nabla_q be the q-connection.

Assume the degree-1 component of \mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{A}) satisfies the integrability condition of \nabla_q. The composition

  \Phi_1^q \circ \mathrm{CMB}
   \colon 
  \pi_0\!\bigl(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}\bigr)
   \longrightarrow 
  \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}(\mathbb{P}(V))

is well-defined. Applying the first Planck step to the CMB of an aeon produces an object with A_0 \neq 0, landing back inside \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}.

Content of the conjecture.

  1. The CMB regenerates particles. Iterating the degree-1 transport data (winding modes) in \mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{A}) once by the Reeb flow f_q produces non-trivial degree-0 fibre data. This makes precise the "condensation" of thermal radiation into particle states.
  2. The recycling map lands in a new aeon. The output \Phi_1^q(\mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{A})) lies in \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}. It inhabits some connected component—a (possibly new) aeon \mathcal{A}'.
  3. Adjacent aeons connect via the recycling map. If \mathcal{A} and \mathcal{A}' are adjacent , then \Phi_1^q(\mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{A})) \in \mathcal{A}'.

The integrability condition. The q-connection \nabla_q defines parallel transport along the Reeb flow. The integrability condition is \nabla_q^2 = F_{\nabla_q}. The connection's curvature determines whether degree-1 data iterates coherently. When F_{\nabla_q} aligns with the degree-2 component of the CMB, the transport data fits together globally. This ensures the recycling map is well-defined.

Categorical formulation. If the conjecture holds for all aeons, \Phi_1^q \circ \mathrm{CMB} extends to a functor:

  \mathcal{R}
   \colon 
  \pi_0(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ})
   \longrightarrow 
  \pi_0(\mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}).

One calls this the recycling functor. It maps each aeon to its successor. A fixed point of \mathcal{R} represents a self-recycling aeon: one whose CMB regenerates itself.
prop:horizon-conformal-invariance:
Proposition Conformal invariance at the jet horizon. Let \mathcal{H} be a jet horizon in an affine chart U. Let A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots denote the brane tower.

The boundary datum \partial\mathcal{A} = (A_1/A_0, A_2/A_0)|_{\mathcal{H}} that survives the horizon is invariant under rescaling of A_0. For any \lambda \in \mathcal{O}(U)^{\times}:

  (A_1 / \lambda A_0, A_2 / \lambda A_0)\big|_{\mathcal{H}}
  = 
  (A_1 / A_0, A_2 / A_0)\big|_{\mathcal{H}}.

Consequently, the boundary datum depends only on the conformal class of A_0 (its zero locus), and not on the specific generator of the horizon ideal \mathfrak{h}.
prf:horizon-conformal-invariance: Proof Proof of horizon conformal invariance. Sketch. On \mathcal{H}, the ideal \mathfrak{h} vanishes: s|_{\mathcal{H}} = 0 for all s \in A_0. The quotient A_k/A_0 restricted to \mathcal{H} depends solely on the equivalence class of sections modulo \mathfrak{h}. Rescaling A_0 \mapsto \lambda A_0 with \lambda|_{\mathcal{H}} \neq 0 preserves the ideal \mathfrak{h}, because \lambda s vanishes on \mathcal{H} if and only if s does. The quotients are therefore identical on \mathcal{H}. \square
rem:horizon-conformal-invariance-interpr:
Remark Conformal invariance at the horizon as a consequence of observability. This provides the QOU analogue to conformal invariance in Penrose's CCC [penrose2010]. In CCC, massless particles are conformally invariant; they do not see the conformal factor \Omega. Here, the degree \geq 1 jet data ignores the "size" of A_0. Only its vanishing locus matters.

The QOU observability axioms require a non-degenerate Frobenius pairing to detect degree-0 data. At the horizon, A_0 = 0 and the Frobenius pairing degenerates on that component. The surviving observations act exclusively on A_k/A_0 — the higher-jet conformal data. Conformal invariance at the horizon emerges as a consequence of the observability axioms, rather than an additional assumption.
prop:qou-is-ccc:
Proposition Aeon boundaries satisfy the horizon-local conditions of a conformal cyclic cosmology. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a QOU. Let U \subset M_0 be an affine chart admitting a chain of adjacent aeons \ldots, \mathcal{A}_{-1}, \mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1, \ldots . This aeon chain satisfies the horizon-local conditions CCC-1 and CCC-3 of a conformal cyclic cosmology [penrose2010]; the inheritance condition CCC-2 is stated as a conjecture and is not part of the formalised statement:

  1. (CCC-1) Conformal invariance at boundaries. At each aeon boundary \mathcal{S}_b, the boundary datum
  \partial\mathcal{A}|_b = (A_1/A_0, A_2/A_0)|_{\mathcal{S}_b}

is invariant under rescaling of A_0, depending only on the conformal class of the horizon ideal \mathfrak{h} — on the vanishing locus, not the specific generator.

  1. (CCC-2) Boundary data inheritance. (Conjectural.) The initial boundary datum of aeon \mathcal{A}_{k+1} precisely matches the terminal boundary datum of aeon \mathcal{A}_k:
  \mathrm{CMB}(\mathcal{S}_0^{(k+1)})
  = 
  \partial\mathcal{A}_k\big|_b.

The degree \geq 1 jet data that survives the terminal horizon of one aeon constitutes the seed of the next.

  1. (CCC-3) Only conformally invariant data crosses. At each boundary, the degree-0 algebra vanishes (A_0|_{\mathcal{S}_b} = 0). By the observability axioms, the Frobenius pairing degenerates on A_0, so no degree-0 observable can detect a difference across the boundary. The only data that crosses is the degree \geq 1 quotient, which is exactly the conformal data.
prf:qou-is-ccc:
Proof Proof of qou is ccc. (CCC-1) constitutes the content of conformal invariance at the jet horizon.

(CCC-2) follows from the definition of aeon adjacency (aeon). Adjacent aeons share the boundary \mathcal{S}_b. The CMB of the successor aeon is exactly the degree \geq 1 data at its past boundary, which is the shared locus \mathcal{S}_b.

(CCC-3) follows from the definition of a jet horizon (jet horizon). The defining condition is A_0|_{\mathcal{H}} = 0. The Frobenius non-degeneracy axiom requires A_0 \neq 0 for well-defined degree-0 observations. At the boundary where A_0 = 0, the pairing degenerates. Consequently, degree-0 data is unobservable. \square

Limitations of the claim. The proposition establishes that a QOU containing aeons is structurally a CCC. It does not claim that any particular affine chart admits aeons (a dynamical question). It does not claim that the aeon chain is infinite. Finally, it does not adopt Penrose's specific conformal metric rescaling g \mapsto \Omega^2 g; the QOU mechanism is ideal vanishing.
rem:penrose-ccc:
Remark Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology. The aeon structure parallels Penrose's Conformal Cyclic Cosmology (CCC) [penrose2010]. The underlying mechanism, however, differs.

Penrose's CCC. In CCC, the infinite future of one aeon is conformally identified with the Big Bang of the next. At t \to \infty, all massive particles have decayed to massless radiation. Massless particles, such as photons and gravitons, are conformally invariant. The conformal structure at t \to \infty is therefore compatible with the conformal structure at t = 0 of the successor aeon. The transition is a conformal rescaling g \mapsto \Omega^2 g with \Omega \to 0.

QOU translation. In the QOU framework, the aeon boundary is a degree-0 vanishing, not a conformal rescaling. The horizon ideal \mathfrak{h} \subset A_0 annihilates all zeroth-order sections.

See Table.

Key differences.

  1. No conformal rescaling. The QOU aeon boundary is algebraic (ideal vanishing), not geometric (metric rescaling). The brane tower structure is preserved across the boundary. Only the lowest floor (A_0) is removed.

  2. The CMB is degree \geq 1 data. In CCC, the CMB of one aeon carries imprints from the previous aeon's final state. In the QOU, this is the boundary datum \partial\mathcal{A}|_b. It consists of the first- and second-order jet data that survives the horizon.

  3. Local, not global. CCC is a global cosmological model with a definite cyclic timeline. The QOU aeon structure is local to an affine chart. Different charts may have different numbers of aeons, or none at all.

  4. Reverse flow. The backward iteration f_q^{-1} of the Reeb dynamics may or may not reach a past boundary (A_0 \to 0). If it does, the affine chart acquires a past jet horizon, representing a big bang state, and the reverse flow terminates. If it does not, the aeon is past-complete and there is no cyclic structure in that chart. Cyclicity is a consequence of dynamics, not an axiom.

sec:swampland-connections-intro:
Specialised to the archimedean ground field k = \mathbb{C}, the rigid axioms of a quantum observable universe structurally align with several consistency criteria of the Swampland Program [vafa2005, palti2019]. This program separates effective field theories admitting a quantum-gravity completion from those that do not.

One records this correspondence as a dictionary, not a derivation. This paper does not model quantum gravity. One makes no claim to settle any Swampland conjecture. Three structures forced by the axioms serve as categorical counterparts to Swampland criteria:

  1. The vanishing of the adjoint invariants \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 corresponds to the absence of exact global symmetries.
  2. The jet horizon (A_0 \to 0) at the foot of the brane tower corresponds to the tower of light states of the Distance Conjecture.
  3. The rigidity of Bring's surface (\chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6) corresponds to the selection of an isolated consistent point in moduli space.

The electromagnetic coupling \alpha_{EM}^{-1} = q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q supplies a fourth entry, aligned with the Emergence Proposal.

In each case, the QOU realises algebraically, and at a single rigid point, what the Swampland Program states asymptotically across a continuous landscape. The categorical structures furnish concrete instances of Swampland pictures. They do not establish the conjectures themselves.
rem:swampland-no-global-symmetry:
Remark Swampland correspondence: observability and the absence of global symmetries. The observability axiom (quantum observable universe, condition ii) requires:

  \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0.

The adjoint object carries no invariant section. This provides the categorical form of a foundational Swampland criterion.

The Swampland statement. A consistent theory of quantum gravity admits no exact global symmetry [banks-seiberg2011]. In holographic settings, this is established rather than conjectural [harlow-ooguri2021]. A global symmetry would act on the matter content while commuting with every local observable. This leaves a sector that no measurement can reach.

QOU translation. The vanishing \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 equates to the vanishing of the zeroth adjoint cohomology H^0_G(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) (quantum observable universe). The Lie algebra of \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) is exactly \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)). The axiom therefore excludes any infinitesimal automorphism of the fibre functor \tau that acts trivially on every observable. This precisely forbids a decoupled global symmetry. Every internal degree of freedom is gauge-accessible to measurement.

Scope. The correspondence is structural. The Swampland statement constrains dynamical gravity based on black-hole physics. Here, the same exclusion is imposed as a categorical axiom, the vanishing of the hom-space \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{C}}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)). The framework does not derive the no-global-symmetry principle of quantum gravity. It internalises the same structural content.
rem:swampland-distance-conjecture:
Remark Swampland correspondence: the brane tower and the Distance Conjecture. The recursive brane tower A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots and its direct-limit algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim_n \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) provide a categorical counterpart of the Swampland Distance Conjecture.

The Swampland statement. Traversing an infinite geodesic distance \Delta\phi in moduli space produces an infinite tower of states whose masses fall exponentially, m \sim m_0\, e^{-c\,\Delta\phi}. The local effective field theory description breaks down [ooguri-vafa2007].

QOU translation. Each jet prolongation J^1(A_n) adds a floor to the tower. Interaction defects of order \geq 3 that cannot be absorbed at level n ascend one jet level at a time. At the jet horizon, the degree-0 algebra vanishes while higher-degree jet data leak through. The fibre-valued particle-identity description fails. Only the tower of higher-order data survives. This serves as the categorical analogue of an effective description breaking down into a surviving tower of states.

Scope. The brane tower, its colimit, and the jet horizon are defined. Identifying the transfinite limit with an infinite-distance point of a moduli space is interpretive. Reading the jet-horizon vanishing A_0 \to 0 as the generic endpoint of that limit is also interpretive. The framework carries no metric moduli space. A global Frobenius degeneration at the limit is not established. The axioms propagate Frobenius non-degeneracy up the tower. One reads the dictionary in one direction. The jet horizon furnishes a concrete instance of the Distance-Conjecture picture, not a proof of it.
rem:swampland-island-of-consistency:
Remark Swampland correspondence: Bring rigidity and the island of consistency. Bring's surface enters the framework as a rigid selection. Its categorical Euler characteristic is fixed:

  \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6

is the genus-4 curve that realises this value. This rigidity provides the QOU counterpart to the Swampland "island of consistency".

The Swampland statement. Within the landscape of effective field theories, only a sparse subset admits a quantum-gravity completion [vafa2005]. Consistency criteria such as the Weak Gravity Conjecture [arkani-hamed2007] carve out the admissible region. This leaves isolated islands rather than a continuum.

QOU translation. Demanding an observable volume fixes the categorical Euler characteristic to \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6. The genus-4 hyperbolic structure realising this value is rigid. By Mostow rigidity [mostow1968], a finite-volume hyperbolic structure of dimension at least three admits no continuous deformation. Therefore, the topological data and the masses derived from it are discrete. The framework occupies an isolated point rather than a continuous family of vacua.

Scope. The identity \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 is proved. The identification of Bring's surface as the terminal genus-4 object is a categorical result. The stronger reading—that this geometric rigidity selects the aether parameter q_0—is motivational, not derived. Calibration against the muon-to-electron mass ratio fixes q_0, not Mostow rigidity. No theorem established here forces q_0 from \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6. Mostow rigidity makes the hyperbolic geometry discrete. It does not, on its own, determine the aether modulus.
rem:swampland-emergent-coupling:
Remark Swampland correspondence: the electromagnetic coupling and the Emergence Proposal. The electromagnetic coupling is not a free input. It is a categorical trace ratio,

  \alpha_{EM} = \frac{h^{2}}{q\,\delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{2,9})\,\delta^{\mathrm{top}}_q(T_{3,5})}.

This exact algebraic identity in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}] is built from the two genus-4-saturating force-carrier torus knots. It echoes the Emergence Proposal.

The Swampland statement. Gauge couplings and kinetic terms are not fundamental. They are generated in the infrared by integrating out a tower of charged states. Weak coupling emerges at large distance in moduli space [heidenreich2018, ooguri-vafa2007].

QOU translation. The discrete topological data of the force-carrier knots generates the coupling, replacing a continuum loop sum. The conclusion remains parallel. The coupling \alpha_{EM} is a derived consequence of the aether. Sending the coupling toward its classical limit forces q \to 1. Here, the skein parameter h = q - q^{-1} vanishes. The braiding degenerates to a symmetric monoidal structure. The topological information distinguishing charged states is erased. This forms the QOU image of weak coupling at the boundary of the parameter space.

Scope. The trace-ratio identity and its combinatorial form \alpha_{EM}^{-1} = q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q are proved. Agreement with the measured value at the aether parameter is leading-order. The remaining high-precision residual awaits a separate Chern–Simons correction. The emergence described here is a structural fact: topology fixes the coupling. This is not a claim that its measured value is fully derived.
sec:quantum-brings:
The quantum deformation of the commutator relations on Bring's surface is described here in outline. The classical commutator [e_a, e_b] = \epsilon_{abc}\,e_c on \mathfrak{su}(2) is replaced by the q-deformed commutator from U_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)). Bring's defining equations \sum x_j = \sum x_j^2 = \sum x_j^3 = 0 are interpreted as relations on the q-symmetric algebra of the aether parameter q(p). This formalism relates the non-commutative geometry of the deformed surface directly to the aether parameter, recovering the classical Bring surface in the limit q \to 1.

The details are not developed here; this section fixes only the structural scope of the deformation.
sec:other-euler:
Bring's surface has analogues at Euler characteristics other than \chi = -6. The classification programme covering \chi = -2, -4, -8, \ldots has three goals: to identify the automorphism groups that arise at each \chi; to determine whether the corresponding observational axioms admit any valid model; and to connect these groups to the aether-parameter dependence on \chi developed earlier.

None of the three is settled here. This section states the programme and fixes its scope; the classification itself is open.
sec:measurement-observation-prose-intro:
This chapter develops the categorical account of quantum measurement within the QOU framework. Consider the most familiar measurement instance: an observer projects a quantum state and reads off a single definite outcome. The fibre functor \tau : \mathbf{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}_{\mathbb{C}} is exactly that operation. It extracts a complex vector space from the categorical state, against which observation projects.

Decoherence, the projective collapse postulate, the Born rule, and the von Neumann measurement model are consequences of how \tau interacts with the rigid-braided aether. This chapter derives each from categorical statements rather than additional postulates.
sec:bundle-observation-intro:
The knot-particle dictionary assigns a particle to each knot composite but leaves the carrier untouched. The carrier is now made explicit. A bundle initial condition fixes the data over the brane, the observation map factors through a braid, and the resulting sorting deposits energy q + q^{-1} per crossing in the colour fibre.

The argument proceeds from the physical reading of the Borromean composite to the bundle initial data it fixes over the brane, and then to observation itself. The load-bearing step proves that sorting deposits energy in the colour fibre—observation is an open braid map whose internal crossings each pay the Hecke-eigenvalue cost. From there the picture acquires dynamics: isotopic bundle data as the same physical state, torsion-driven flow through configuration space, and its categorical home as finite bundles over \mathbb{P}(V).
rem:quarks-borromean-picture:
Remark Quarks and hadrons in the Borromean picture. Quarks are Borromean-linked unknots rather than individual knot types. The quarks are unknots (neutrinos) Borromean-linked in the exceptional divisor of Bring's surface, and a baryon is the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3(\nu_r, \nu_g, \nu_b) bound by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H:

  • Proton: \mathcal{B}_3(\nu_r, \nu_g, \nu_b) \oplus \mathcal{L}_H with the 2 + 1 crossing-orientation partition (two up, one down).
  • Neutron: \mathcal{B}_3(\nu_r, \nu_g, \nu_b) \oplus \mathcal{L}_H with the 1 + 2 partition (one up, two down).

Up/down flavour arises from the crossing orientation of each unknot within \mathcal{B}_3, not from distinct knot types. The Borromean complement has hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3) = 7.328\ldots.

Under the pair Skein formula the proton and neutron masses are an invertible function of two dressed quark masses, so the formula reproduces the measured values once those two masses are chosen; it does not predict them.
def:bundle-initial-conditions:
Definition Bundle initial conditions. Let \mathbb{P}(V) be the projective line, with a reference point in an affine chart. A bundle initial condition is a formal sum of localized hadrons and photons at base points,

  \mathcal{S}_0 = \sum_{i \in I} (p_i, H_i),

where each (p_i, H_i) is a localized hadron or a photon, the index set I may be infinite, and multiple constituents may share the same base point.
rem:bundle-initial-conditions-remark:
Remark Bundle initial conditions as position-only data. A measurement records where each constituent sits on the fibre while leaving its momentum entirely free; a bundle initial condition encodes exactly this position-only data. The photon identity \mathbf{1}_{B_4} is knot-trivial under Markov closure yet carries four internal polarisation/chirality components on the exceptional divisor.

Equivalently, \mathcal{S}_0 is a section of the free commutative monoid on the hadron sheaf \mathcal{H}:

  \mathcal{S}_0 \in \Gamma\!\bigl(\mathbb{P}(V), \mathrm{Free}_{\mathrm{CMon}}(\mathcal{H})\bigr).

This specifies the fibre data of the bundle—which constituent sits in which fibre—without any information about the horizontal transport connecting neighbouring fibres.

Subsequent configurations \mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2, \ldots represent the forward light cone from \mathcal{S}_0. Each step applies one iteration of the Reeb flow, adding horizontal transport and accumulating interaction relations. The backward sequence represents the past light cone.
rem:observation-braid:
Remark Observation as an open map: crossing injection and input. An observation injects genuinely new information. Its outcome is not necessarily determined by the initial conditions \mathcal{S}_0. This is the open-map property: observation maps open sets in the state space to open sets, creating new open neighbourhoods not present in \mathcal{S}_0.

In the braid picture, an observation inserts a new crossing into the braid word. The crossing type is not forced by the existing braid. Each observation is one crossing injected at a discrete Planck step, supplying one bit of information.

The Toffoli gate requires three crossings. An observer performing one Toffoli computation injects three crossings into the braid, corresponding to three Planck steps of intentional interaction with the state bundle.
sec:observation-intention-prose:
Je pense, donc je suis. — René Descartes, Discours de la méthode (1637)

An observation is an intentional act within the state bundle rather than a passive reading from outside it. Formally, the observation morphism \mathfrak{O} \in \Gamma(U, \mathrm{Ad}(J^1\mathcal{S})) acts as an open braid map that injects crossings into the horizontal transport of the bundle, perturbing the aether parameter by \delta q > 0 per crossing. Each intentional sorting step rotates a disordered pair from the antisymmetric eigenspace \bigwedge^2(V) (eigenvalue -q^{-1}) to the symmetric eigenspace \mathrm{Sym}^2(V) (eigenvalue q), depositing the fixed Hecke-eigenvalue gap q + q^{-1} into the colour fibre and driving the torsion-knot flow across \mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V)).
rem:observation-intent-energy:
Remark Intent and the energetic cost of observation. Choosing to sort a sequence of items inserts crossings that increase local order (decreasing classical entropy) at the cost of quantum energy (\delta q > 0 per crossing). Every observation costs at least one crossing's worth of \hbar_q.

An observation is done with intent. Physically, intent increases the quantum energy of the system. The aether perturbation \delta q > 0 shifts q upward, increasing the quantum Planck constant \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}. The crossing energy of the injected crossing is the energetic cost of the observation.

The intent can either increase or decrease the classical energy of the system provided the change is continuous. It cannot leave the quantum energy unchanged.
rem:observation-braid-not-predetermined:
Remark The braid is not predetermined: flow versus observation. The initial conditions \mathcal{S}_0 specify fibre data without horizontal transport. The braid that unfolds from \mathcal{S}_0 encodes the horizontal transport. Observations modify this braid in real time. The full braid word of the universe interleaves two sources:

  1. The flow: Crossings generated by the autonomous Reeb dynamics of the state bundle, determined by \mathcal{S}_0 and the variational equations.
  2. Observations: Crossings injected by observers via the adjoint action on the colour fibre, determined by open-map contributions, not by \mathcal{S}_0.

Suppose the flow winds three colour fibres into \sigma_1\sigma_2. An observer measuring the first and third strands injects a single inverse crossing \sigma_1^{-1}, completing the word to \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1^{-1}. No autonomous continuation of \mathcal{S}_0 would have produced this finite braid. The observation does not perturb the flow; it appends a crossing the flow could not.

The open map structure of observation implies that the set of reachable sections is larger than the set determined by the initial conditions alone.
prop:sorting-color-energy:
Proposition Sorting deposits energy q + q^{-1} per crossing in the colour fibre. Observation sorts colour. Swapping two adjacent items into their correct order is a projection between the two eigenspaces of the R-matrix. Each swap deposits a fixed quantum of energy in the colour fibre.

Let \sigma_i be the Hecke generator acting on V \otimes V, where V is the fundamental representation. Then:

  1. (Eigenspace decomposition.) The R-matrix decomposes V \otimes V into two eigenspaces:

      V \otimes V = \mathrm{Sym}^2(V) \oplus \textstyle\bigwedge^2(V)

    with eigenvalues q (symmetric, ordered) and -q^{-1} (antisymmetric, disordered) respectively.

  2. (Sorting is projection.) A sorting operation is the projection from \bigwedge^2(V) to \mathrm{Sym}^2(V) at the generator \sigma_i. This projection acts on the colour fibre by rotating the gauge degrees of freedom from the disordered to the ordered eigenspace.

  3. (Energy per crossing.) The energy deposited in the colour fibre by one sorting operation is the eigenvalue gap:

      \Delta E_{\mathrm{colour}} = q - (-q^{-1}) = q + q^{-1}

    At q = q_0, \Delta E = 2.011 action units per crossing.

  4. (Total sorting energy.) Let \pi \in S_n be a permutation representing the disordered state of n items. The minimum number of adjacent transpositions needed to sort \pi is the inversion count \mathrm{inv}(\pi). The total energy deposited is:

      E_{\mathrm{colour}}(\pi) = \mathrm{inv}(\pi) \cdot (q + q^{-1})

prf:sorting-color-energy:
Proof Proof of sorting color energy. Sorting deposits energy because a disordered pair sits in the antisymmetric eigenspace at eigenvalue -q^{-1}, and sorting lifts it to the symmetric eigenspace at eigenvalue q; the exchange must therefore pay the gap between the two. This is made precise by computing the projections onto each eigenspace.

(1) The Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 - (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i - 1 = 0 has roots q and -q^{-1} by the quadratic formula. The corresponding idempotents are:

  e_+ = \frac{\sigma_i + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}, \qquad
  e_- = \frac{q - \sigma_i}{q + q^{-1}}

with e_+ + e_- = 1 and e_+ e_- = 0. The image of e_+ is \mathrm{Sym}^2(V) (the symmetric representation, eigenvalue q); the image of e_- is \bigwedge^2(V) (the antisymmetric representation, eigenvalue -q^{-1}).

(2) A disordered pair occupies \bigwedge^2(V): the two items are in the wrong order, so the state is antisymmetric under exchange. Sorting swaps them into the correct order, moving the state to \mathrm{Sym}^2(V). This is the projection e_+. In the observation (observation), e_+ is the \mathrm{Ad} component: it acts on the colour fibre by conjugation, rotating the antisymmetric state to the symmetric eigenspace.

(3) The energy deposited is the eigenvalue difference: q - (-q^{-1}) = q + q^{-1}.

(4) Each adjacent transposition in the sorting algorithm corresponds to one braid crossing \sigma_i. The standard result from combinatorics: the minimum number of adjacent transpositions to realise \pi equals \mathrm{inv}(\pi), the number of pairs (i, j) with i < j and \pi(i) > \pi(j). Each crossing deposits q + q^{-1} in the colour fibre. \square

def:bundle-isotopy-equivalence:
Definition Isotopy equivalence of bundle initial conditions. Two bundle initial conditions are isotopy equivalent if they are related by a permutation of indices and an ambient isotopy within each fibre:

  \{(p_i, H_i)\}_{i \in I} \sim \{(p_{\sigma(i)}, H_{\sigma(i)}')\}_{i \in I}

where \sigma is a bijection on I and each H_{\sigma(i)}' is ambient-isotopic to H_{\sigma(i)} in the fibre E_{p_{\sigma(i)}}.
rem:bundle-isotopy-equivalence-remark: Remark Why bundle initial conditions are taken up to isotopy. The physical content of a bundle initial condition depends only on which hadron types are placed where, not on the index labels or the particular representative of each ambient isotopy class; isotopy equivalence identifies exactly the conditions with the same content.
def:torsion-knot-flow:
Definition Torsion-driven knot flow. Given a bundle initial condition \mathcal{S}_0 = \{(p_i, K_i)\}_{i=1}^{N}, the torsion-driven knot flow is the one-parameter family of bundle states

  \mathcal{S}_t = \bigl\{\bigl(\Phi_t^q(p_i), K_i\bigr)\bigr\}_{i=1}^{N} \qquad t \geq 0,

where \Phi_t^q is the flow on \mathbb{P}(V) generated by the q-deformed Reeb vector field \xi_q.

The flow has two components.

  1. Intrinsic rotation. Each knot type K carries an intrinsic angular momentum proportional to its crossing number c(K):

      \omega_K = c(K) \cdot \frac{2\pi}{[c(K)]_q!}

  2. Pairwise interaction. When two localized knots (p_i, K_i) and (p_j, K_j) are within Planck-scale separation d_{\mathbb{P}(V)}(p_i, p_j) < \ell_P, they experience a short-range repulsive force

      F_{ij} = \frac{\Delta_q(K_i) \cdot \Delta_q(K_j)}{d(p_i, p_j)^2 + \ell_P^2}

    where \Delta_q(K) is the q-Alexander polynomial of K evaluated at q = e^{-r}.
